title: VPC + Branch/On‑Prem Satellite Deployment Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose
This playbook documents Redwood Inference’s recommended approach for deploying a small-footprint private inference deployment that spans a central VPC control plane and one or more branch or on‑prem satellite sites ("branch sites"). It is intended for field engineers, SREs, and customer platform teams responsible for initial installs and ongoing day‑2 operations.

Scope and assumptions
- Target use case: customers that need local inference capacity (low-latency for local users, data locality, or regulatory reasons) but want a unified control plane in a VPC.
- Branch footprint: 1–4 GPUs (A100/RTX class), lightweight orchestrator (k3s/k8s edge), limited storage (100–500GB model cache), and optional airgap support.
- Network: branch sites have constrained egress and may rely on a NAT/proxy. Control-plane connectivity uses mTLS tunnels or customer VPN.
- Security: branches should integrate with customer KMS where available or use HSM-backed secrets in the control plane.

High-level architecture
1) Central control plane (VPC)
   - Responsibilities: model distribution, billing/telemetry aggregation, global routing policies, and rollouts.
   - Services: control-plane-api, model-registry, model-distributor, rollout-orchestrator, telemetry-collector.
2) Branch site (satellite)
   - Responsibilities: local inference serving runtime, KV cache for session state, local observability agent, local ingress for customer traffic.
   - Components: runtime agent, model cache, sidecar proxy, local metrics forwarder.
3) Connectivity patterns
   - Preferred: TLS mTLS tunnel from branch to VPC with mutual auth and port-restricted egress.
   - Alternate: Site-to-site VPN with route only to control-plane CIDRs.

SLOs and operational targets (branch level)
- Inference P95 latency (local routing): < 75ms for short prompt workloads (<=512 tokens).
- Availability: 99.5% per branch (monthly).
- Model-sync success rate: >= 99.9% for scheduled sync windows.
- Telemetry delivery: >= 95% of metrics delivered within 5 minutes.

Preparation checklist (pre‑install)
- Customer signoff: hardware SKU list, firmware versions, network egress rules, and approved maintenance windows.
- Hostnames and DNS: reserve branch hostnames and local FQDNs.
- Certificates: generate branch CSR and submit to control-plane CA or confirm use of provided client certificates.
- KMS integration: coordinate key wrap/unwrap approach; confirm HSM reachability if used.
- Acceptance tests: confirm required ports (see Table 1), enough disk for model cache, and GPU drivers installed.

Table 1 — Required network egress (example)
- TCP 443 to control-plane-api.redwood.internal
- TCP 5222 (mTLS tunnel) to model-distributor.redwood.internal
- UDP 500/4500 (if using IPSec VPN)
- Optional: TCP 9000 for telemetry aggregator (if not proxied)

Deployment steps (initial install)
1) Field preparation (on‑site)
   - Verify hardware inventory and run hardware-selfcheck script: sudo /opt/redwood/bin/hw-check.sh
   - Ensure drivers: nvidia-smi shows supported driver >= 525.xx
2) Bootstrap edge orchestrator
   - For k3s: curl -sfL https://get.k3s.io | INSTALL_K3S_VERSION=v1.27 sh -
   - Label node: kubectl label node <node> redwood/branch=true
3) Install runtime packages
   - Apply RBAC and service accounts: kubectl apply -f rbac-branch.yaml
   - Deploy runtime: kubectl apply -f runtime-deployment-branch.yaml
   - Confirm pods Ready: kubectl get pods -n redwood-runtime
4) Establish control plane connectivity
   - Install the mTLS tunnel agent and provision the cert: redwoodctl enroll --csr /tmp/branch.csr --target control-plane
   - Verify tunnel up: redwoodctl tunnel status --verbose
5) Model sync and warmup
   - Start scheduled model-sync job: kubectl apply -f branch-model-sync-cron.yaml
   - Warmup step: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/internal/warmup -d '{"model":"redwood-7b", "prompt":"<warmup>"}'
6) Post-install acceptance tests (automated)
   - Run acceptance script: /opt/redwood/bin/branch-acceptance.sh --suite basic
   - Validate local inference: run sample inference against local ingress and assert latency and correctness thresholds.

Rollback and upgrade strategy
- Goal: enable zero-to-minimal traffic-impact upgrades for branch runtime and model swaps.
- Pattern: Canary -> Staged Rollout -> Auto-fallback.

Runtime upgrade steps (recommended)
1) Canary (one branch node)
   - Quiesce non-critical workloads: redwoodctl scale --replicas 0 --selector noncritical=true
   - Deploy new runtime image with same API contract: kubectl set image deploy/runtime redwood/runtime:<new-tag>
   - Monitor health for 15 minutes (check CPU/GPU utilization, p95 latency).
2) Staged rollout (remaining branches)
   - Use rollout-orchestrator to progress to groups of branches (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%).
   - Target low-traffic windows for each group.
3) Automatic fallback
   - If model-serving error rate > 2% or P95 latency increases > 2x for 10 minutes, rollback automatically: rollout-orchestrator rollback <rollout-id>

Stateful model swap and rollback
- Model swaps must preserve KV cache compatibility. Strategy: model-compatibility layer + prefix-based cache versioning.
- Steps to swap a model at branch:
  1. Upload model to model-registry with a new semantic version.
  2. Trigger model-distributor to push delta: redwoodctl model push --branch <branch-id> --model redwood-13b:v2
  3. Start traffic-splitting at runtime with 5% diverted to v2 for 10 minutes.
  4. If regressions, revert traffic-split to v1 and schedule a patch.

Failure modes and mitigation (day 2)
- Partial model corruption during sync
  - Detection: checksum mismatch alerts and model-start failures.
  - Mitigation: keep a two-version on-disk cache, fall back to previous version immediately, mark branch degraded and re-enqueue model sync.
- Network blackouts (branch loses control-plane)
  - Behavior: local inference continues for cached models; control-plane dependent features (global rollouts, new model fetches) blocked.
  - Recovery: local agent buffers telemetry and reconciles on reconnect. If control-plane unreachable > 12 hours, escalate to SRE and advise customer to check network routes.
- Noisy neighbor GPU starvation
  - Detection: prolonged GPU saturation with high queue depth.
  - Mitigation: apply per-tenant QoS in runtime, optionally autoscale ephemeral worker containers or bleed noncritical workloads.

Operational playbook (incident template)
1) Triage: collect branch id, control-plane tunnel status, recent model-sync logs, and telemetry window (last 30m).
2) Immediate actions (if severe impact): revert recent rollouts, pause model-syncs, and throttle incoming traffic via control-plane routing policy.
3) Remediation: restore corrected model or runtime, validate with unit prompts, and run smoke tests.
4) Postmortem: update branch runbook, add new acceptance tests if gap was in validation.

Day‑2 automation and maintenance tasks
- Weekly: verify model cache TTLs and storage consumption; rotate ephemeral keys monthly.
- Monthly: perform a staged runtime image upgrade in a canary branch and validate.
- Quarterly: exercise full offline-scenario failover (simulate control-plane unavailability for 4h).

Acceptance criteria checklist (customer sign-off)
- Network egress confirmed and certs validated.
- Local inference P95 under agreed SLA for baseline prompts.
- Model sync completes for first three models without error.
- Telemetry consumed in control plane and sample traces visible in Console.

Useful CLI snippets
- Enroll branch: redwoodctl enroll --branch-id BR-001 --csr /tmp/branch.csr --control-plane https://api.redwood.internal
- Check model sync status: redwoodctl model status --branch BR-001 --model redwood-7b
- Force rollback: redwoodctl rollout rollback --rollout-id r-2026-03-15-01 --reason "regression: latency spike"

Ownership and escalation
- Primary owner: Private Deployments Field Engineering (contact: private-deploy@redwood.ai).
- Secondary owner: Eng SRE (oncall pager: +1-555-0100).
- Escalation path: Field Eng -> SRE -> Runtime Team -> Platform Security; use #private-deploy-alerts Slack channel for communications.

References and related reading
- See reference-architectures/edge-gateway-and-airgapped-bridge-architecture for network patterns.
- See onprem-packaging/airgap-packaging-and-day2-hardening for image signing and offline installs.
- See day-2-ops/kv-cache-migrations-and-runtime-state-migration-playbook for deep-dive on cache migrations.

Appendix A — Branch validation script (example)
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
echo "Running branch acceptance checks..."
# Check GPU
if ! command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "nvidia-smi not found"; exit 2
fi
echo "GPU drivers present:"; nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name --format=csv
# Smoke inference
curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","prompt":"Hello"}' | jq '.status'

echo "All done"
